name: Regroupement Familial (Family reunification)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor to have held a residence permit for at least 18 months.
requirements.fix_path: Wait until the sponsor reaches the required tenure.

value.note: resources at least equal to SMIC, scaling with family size

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor's resources to be at least equal to the SMIC, scaling upward with family size.
requirements.fix_path: Increase income to the required level.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires housing considered adequate for the family size, per local standards.

requirement_groups.name: Vie Privée et Familiale — family of a French citizen

requirements.blocker_text: This covers spouses and family members of French citizens, and does not carry the same income/housing prerequisites or sponsor-tenure wait as the standard regroupement familial route.

evidence_required.document: Marriage/partnership certificate or birth certificate proving family tie
Sponsor's income and housing evidence (standard route only)

sources.title: Légifrance — CESEDA, regroupement familial and vie privée et familiale provisions

notes: Modeled with two genuinely distinct groups: standard regroupement familial (sponsor not French, income/housing tests apply, 18-month sponsor-tenure wait) and the 'Vie Privée et Familiale' category specifically for family of FRENCH citizens, which does not carry the same prerequisites — a real structural distinction, similar in spirit to the Netherlands' separate EU-family-member route vs standard family reunification, or Germany's FreizügG/EU vs standard Ehegattennachzug. citizenship_after_months for the family-of-French-citizen group uses 48 months via fr_declaration_mariage's shorter marriage-based path rather than the standard 60-month naturalisation track, reflecting that most people in this group would realistically pursue citizenship via marriage declaration rather than the general residence-based naturalisation route. SMIC-based income threshold formula-linked to the same national variable used across fr_talent routes indirectly (via the fixed talent reference) — though this route's threshold moves with SMIC directly, unlike the talent salary reference, which is now decoupled — a genuine internal inconsistency in the French system worth surfacing: some French thresholds track SMIC live, others (like Talent) don't anymore.
